text: The model flagged the applicant as high‑risk because of three key signals it sees as warning signs. First, the borrower has been 90 days or more past due on a debt twice; each of those serious delinquencies adds a large amount to the risk score (a +2.45 contribution). Second, there are three instances of being 30‑59 days past due, which also push the score upward (+1.81). Finally, the borrower is using about 48 % of the available revolving credit, and that level of utilization adds a smaller but still positive amount (+0.34). Together, these three factors drive the model’s estimate of a 97.6 % chance of default, resulting in the “high risk” decision.
